assertions.name: split_is_at_most_1_6_percent_of_the_energy_at_A63
assertions.source: (r-1)/A at A=63 with a factor-2 flux ratio. The combined relative slack of any two-sided bound must beat this for the interval to be narrower than the split it is meant to explain.

assertions.name: budget_tightens_with_A_by_exactly_A_max_over_A_min
assertions.source: 63/3 = 21. The precision requirement sharpens 21-fold across the ladder, so the route gets harder where the data is best, not easier.

assertions.name: budget_is_strictly_decreasing_in_A
assertions.source: checked across all 31 rungs rather than read off the formula, so a future change to the ladder cannot silently break the monotonicity the reading depends on.

assertions.name: no_ropelength_or_ideal_knot_source_in_the_repo
assertions.source: LIVE scan of docs/, computations/, content/ and library/ (both the sections/ and ocr/ tiers, all library directories). Zero. Asserted so that acquiring such a source FLIPS this assertion and prompts a revisit -- rather than this probe asserting a remembered absence. Note the precision argument does not depend on this: acquisition would not rescue the route.

description: EXPLORATORY. Asks whether acquiring an energy UPPER bound would rescue the Freedman-He route, and finds it would not -- for a reason needing no carrier, no flux value and no acquisition. A two-sided bound pins the mirror split to an interval of width (U1-B1)+(U2-B2), the SUM of the two slacks; but the split is a difference of two large nearly-equal energies, at most (r-1)/A of the energy when the two fluxes lie within a factor r. So the combined relative slack must beat (r-1)/A -- 1.6% at A=63 for r=2, and TIGHTENING with A. Freedman-He-type bounds are order-of-magnitude. Also scans the repo live: zero ropelength / ideal-knot material anywhere, asserted so that a future acquisition flips the assertion instead of this going stale. Companion to QOU/Mass/MirrorSplitIsASmallFractionOfTheEnergy.lean. Nothing wired.

the_arithmetic.interval_width: (U1 - B1) + (U2 - B2)  -- the SUM of the two slacks
the_arithmetic.model: dE = c*(Phi_p - Phi_n) against E = c*(Z*Phi_p + N*Phi_n), d = 1

headline.reading: the requirement SHARPENS with A by exactly the ratio A_max/A_min; a bigger nucleus is a harder target, not an easier one
